title: Cougar Soccer Camp for boys and girls set for July 26-30
description:
The Cranford High School boys and girls soccer programs, in conjunction with Central Jersey Celtic F.A., present their 2010 Cougar Soccer Camp at Orange Avenue School fields during the week of July 26 through July 30. The camp will run from 9:00am-1:00pm and is open for all boys and girls in grades 1-8, from beginners to advanced.

Camp directors are Cranford boys Head Varsity coach Mike Curci, girls Head Varsity coach Jen Michewitz, and P.J. Keim, President of the Central Jersey F.A.

Curci, honored as 2007 Star-Ledger Coach of the Year in Union County, led the CHS boys' varsity team to the Union County Tournament Championship in 2009, the first in the 54-year history of the program. The Cougars also nailed down their third consecutive Mountain Valley Conference Championship, while posting a record-setting 22-1-2 mark, finishing with a # 7 ranking in the Star-Ledger final Top-20. The 2009 team closed the season at 15-6 despite the loss of seven starters to graduation. The 2008 squad finished 9-1 in conference play, and own a conference record of 28-2 over the last three seasons. The 2007 team also finished with 15 wins while posting the first championship of any kind in the fifty-year history of the program. Over the last two seasons, the Cougars are 52-11-3. Curci, entering his 6th season at CHS, began his coaching career by spending several years as an assistant to the legendary Gene Chyzowych of Columbia High School, the all-time winningest coach in state history. Curci led the Columbia J.V. to a 17-0 mark in his 2nd season there before taking over the varsity program at Livingston H.S. where the Lancers made the state tournament all five years while facing perennial powers Columbia, Seton Hall Prep and St. Benedict's. Curci's playing career includes a conference championship at Carteret High School, before becoming a four-year starter at midfield for Seton Hall University where he led the team in goals his junior season and was named captain his senior season. In Coach C.'s five years at the helm, Cranford has gone from 35 players to 90 student/athletes wearing the white, blue and gold at the varsity, J.V. and freshmen levels. The Cougars look forward to building on their county and conference championship seasons as they continue a tradition of excellence. Mike has called Cranford home for the past 20 years with his wife Sally and their four children.

Michewitz is entering her 3rd season as girls Head Varsity Soccer Coach at Cranford. She guided the Lady Cougars to the Union County Championship in 2009, posting victories over rivals Scotch Plains and Westfield in the final two county games en route to a 16-3 record. Michewitz is a graduate of Seton Hall University where she started on the women's soccer team as a defender all 74 games of her career and was a captain her junior and senior years. In 2002, she received honorable mention for the Freshmen All-American Team, and in 2007 she earned the "Woman of the Year" Award from Seton Hall University for her accomplishments in athletics, academics and community service. Jen grew up in Pottstown, PA where she was highly involved with the Eastern Pennsylvania Soccer Association, training youth teams and coaching soccer camps. She currently lives in Westfield and teaches math at Cranford High School.

PJ Keim is President of  Central Jersey Football Academy, which currently supplies trainers to many of the local soccer clubs. He has been coaching youth soccer for over 12 years. Keim is the head coach of the two-time state cup finalist CWS Red Devils. PJ has lived in Cranford for 18 years and is the father of three wonderful children.

Once again, Mark Dutton, of Central Jersey F.A., will join the camp as Director of Coaching. His goal is to provide a positive and safe learning environment for all ages to become stronger athletes. Mark has been running camps in the U.S. for the past 12 years. Former star CHS players will also be on-hand to share their expertise and skills.

For more information or for a camp brochure, please call Mike Curci at 908-294-2101 or PJ Keim at 908-591-6734, or email mscurci@aol.com. You can also go to www.cjceltic.com to register.

title: Visions of Southern France, Saint Tropez & Southport By Henri Lepetit
description:
Born in Brussels in 1956 Henri Lepetit is almost larger then life, an Indiana Jones character who seems to have done everything, from bagging spitting cobras in the Ivory Coast when he was only 13 to fighting in a Squadron of the S.A.S! With skydiving an ongoing hobby he has been a world adventurer who has extracted every possible emotion from his incredibly varied lifestyle. Art has always had a dominant place in his life and this natural talent means that from the early age of 16 he paid for many of his world trips by painting and selling his works en route. With no formal art education he has always had to rely on the public at large to be his severest critic. What you see here are images from Southport Connecticut, Paris, Saint Tropez and Southern France.

title: Conservatory Offers Summer Dance Programs
description:
The Ridgefield Conservatory of Dance has summer dance programs for all age levels that include regular classes as well as two-week workshops.

From July 19 to July 30 the conservatory will  host a Junior Dance Workshop for 7 to 10-year-olds and a Summer Dance Workshop for 11 and up. Junior Dance Workshop provides young dancers with two weeks of daily classes in ballet, jazz, and modern that culminate in a performance for invited guests.

"Dancers improve quickly from the focus of daily classes in a positive environment," says school director James Robey. "The Junior Dance Workshop and the Summer Dance Workshop are some of our most popular programs."

Summer Dance Workshop provides intermediate dancers with two weeks of classes in ballet, jazz and modern. Dancers take 3 classes daily and enjoy the training of an intensive program in a non-competitive environment. Summer Dance Workshop culminates in a performance for invited guests.

In addition to these two programs, the conservatory offers weekly ballet, modern, and jazz classes for 12 year old students and up on Tuesdays and Thursdays throughout the month of July; pre-ballet classes for 3 and 4-year-olds on Tuesday and Thursday mornings; and the annual Ridgefield Summer Intensive for two weeks in August for advanced students 12 years old and up.

title: Family Caregiver of the Year Award
description:
Many families and individuals are caregivers to a loved-one who is afflicted with an illness, an injury - or most commonly - an elder. These caregivers can be daughters, sons, parents, spouses, siblings, other relatives, or even a friend of the person in need.  

According to the National Family Caregivers Association (NFCA) family caregivers represent 80% of all home care services. Due to the humility of many of these dedicated individuals, the everyday sacrifices of family caregivers are often unrecognized and under-appreciated.  

Homewatch CareGivers of Essex, Morris & Union will be recognizing one individual from Essex, Morris County or N. Union Counties who will accept their award at a luncheon at  Eden Gourmet's "ABOVE" restaurant in South Orange, NJ. In addition, he or she will be presented with a gift basket from Eden Gourmet, a gift certificate for dining at "ABOVE", and a 1-hour massage at the Bodhi Tree. We will also award a scholarship to our Homewatch CareGivers University, a professionally developed online training platform designed to reinforce and provide extended training to our employees.

Local winners throughout the country will also eligible to win the "National Family Caregiver of the Year" $5000 grand prize.  

Both local and national winners will be chosen by a select panel of caregiving experts. Our local panel will include Lisa Cook Bayer, J.D. CCM of LMR Eldercare, Margo Montague, Elder Care Advisor for "A Place for Mom", Karen Frank, PT and owner of Back Home Safely as well as Larry Aronson, owner of Homewatch Caregivers. 

Nominees for the "Family Caregiver of the Year" program will be accepted beginning June 22, 2010 through July 27, 2010. A winner will be selected by a local panel of care experts by Sept. 1, 2010. Local winners will also be entered in to the national awards program with selection announced on October 25th, 2010 to highlight November as National Family Caregiver Month awareness month.

Applications are available at Homewatch Caregivers, 75 South Orange Ave, South Orange, NJ,  by calling (973)810-0110 or online at http://tiny.cc/cyvl3 .

title: Union County Parks "Family Flix" Summer Film Series
description:
The Union County Board of Chosen Freeholders and the Department of Parks & Community Renewal are happy to announce that the "Family Flix" summer film series will continue on Tuesday evening, July 27, in Meisel Park.

"Family Flix begin at dusk, but come early to the park to enjoy interesting preview activities at 7:15 p.m. that are fun for the whole family," said Freeholder Vice Chairman Deborah Scanlon, liaison to the Parks and Recreation Advisory Board. "Bring a blanket or beach chair to claim your spot on the lawn or save a seat in the bleachers – either way, the early birds are sure to like the preview activity before each movie."

The next film this summer will be the 1979 musical comedy adventure, "The Muppet Movie," about Kermit the Frog, Fozzie Bear, Miss Piggy and an eccentric cast of characters who trek across America to find success in Hollywood. "The Muppet Movie" will be shown outdoors, free of charge at Meisel Park in Springfield on Tuesday, July 27. There will be a paper-bag puppet-making project for children of all ages at 7:15 p.m., before the movie.

The other dates for Family Flix free outdoor movies are:

title: Chinese Programs in New Canaan
description: Students Participate in Chinese Art and Culture Programs -- Redding-based Artist Introduces Children to Chinese-Themed Mixed-Media Art -- “VP Art & Culture Katy Chen Myers is an energetic, true professional, dedicated to exploring Chinese history and culture with students via art, and we are all so lucky to have her,” noted CLSC Principal, Daisy Chen Laone. Riverside, CT, July 1, 2010 – The Chinese Language School of Connecticut (www.ChineseLanguageSchool.org), the fully-accredited, non-profit, Riverside, CT-based provider of Chinese language programs to students, schools and corporations, is pleased to announce expansion of their preschool, tutoring, and Art and Culture programs for academic year 2010 - 2011. New Canaan resident, Susan Serven, explained, “Many New Canaan parents have expressed interest in our preschool Chinese classes, as well as After School programs and our Art & Culture Workshops, but they may not have been able to make the trip down to Greenwich on weekends or during the school week. We’re pleased to announce that we will now be able to offer our programs at various locations in the New Canaan area, along with private tutoring for NCHS students needing additional practice with their Chinese.” During the Art and Culture section of CLSC’s classes this year, VP Art & Culture Katy Chen Myers, of Redding, CT, developed and ran segments whereby students studied traditions and celebrations focused on Chinese folktales and festivals such as the Moon festival. Handcrafted lanterns have been designed by CLSC students for an art shows in Westport and Greenwich this fall and winter. Ms. Myers explained, Children love to cook, and eat, and are usually very interested in what others’ meals are like, as well. In our segment “The Chinese Diet” we studied agricultural traditions of northern and southern China, culminating with a look at traditional Chinese foods, and the banquet foods of the Qing Dynasty. China has a tradition of travelling performers creating shadow puppet theaters during the Ming Dynasty, and up to the modern era. Our younger students were able to design their own shadow puppets as they learned about these Chinese entertainment traditions. We created our own, authentic traveling Chinese Shadow Puppet theater, probably the only one in the tri-state area, and students assisted in recent puppet performances.” Ms. Myers continued, “One of our goals is to introduce Chinese as a second language to students while allowing them to explore Chinese culture via art in age appropriate ways. Our older students’ main focus centered on answering the question: Who am I? by creating a mixed-media project which involved students telling their own story by creating a biography in Chinese characters, and by creating self portraits using the graphic novel “American Born Chinese by Gene Yang as their inspiration. Another project for this upcoming school year is the Chinese Cherry & plum blossom quilt which will also be readied for exhibit in upcoming shows. One of the highlights of this past year was that in addition to showcasing work at various children’s venues, art created by CLSC students was accepted into a professional artist exhibit at Weston Art’s Center in Weston CT. The seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove, a series of four paintings by students from CLSC levels 3-8, was displayed alongside works by professional illustrators, photographers and print makers from all over the US. We are currently working with various venues to plan more exhibits as professionals, in New Canaan, Ridgefield and New York City for the 2010-2011 academic year. The main theme for CLSC’s art and culture segments next year will be the Silk Road. Many exciting projects are currently being planned for all levels with the goal being exhibition in various schools and libraries in Fairfield County. I’m so pleased to be able to share my passion for art, and Chinese culture, with students of all ages, via CLSC’s programs. ” For information on CLSC’s weekend or weekday language classes, summer programs, private tutoring, corporate services, or any of their other programs, please visit www.ChineseLanguageSchool.org or email them at info@ChineseLanguageSchool.org. * * *

description:
This summer, high school students are invited to experience adventure, fun and meaningful experiences on a Young Life* summer camp trip this July 27 - August 2 at Rockbridge Alum Springs, one of Young Life's  resort-style properties located in the Shenandoah Valley near Lexington, VA.  Get more information and download registration at www.wiltonct.younglife.org 

Local teenagers and Young Life alumni often cite Young Life summer trips as "the best week of their lives."  Throughout this one-of-a-kind week, high school students have fun, build new friendships with peers and local adult leaders and enjoy meaningful and lasting experiences which help shape their character, self-confidence, and leadership potential.

A Local High School Junior says, "Young Life is a place where friends can get together to hang out, discuss life, and the Christian faith in an environment where we don't feel judged and we're free to be ourselves. It's a place where anyone, regardless of who they are or what they believe in, can come and have a good time in a safe, fun and relaxing situation.  Young Life summer camp was without a doubt the best week of my life."

Activities and facilities include white water rafting, high ropes course, climbing tower, zipline, giant water slides, mountain biking, beach volleyball, frisbee golf, pool and hot-tub, game room, athletic fields, gymnasium, tennis and basketball courts, skate park, the "blob", first-class accommodations and lodging and more.  The trip also includes Young Life Clubs featuring live music, hilarious entertainment and relevant talks about life and the Christian faith. See Rockbridge @ www.rockbridge.younglife.org

All teens are invited to participate in Young Life at any level at anytime.  There is no membership or previous participation needed. 

* Young Life is a non-profit organization committed to impacting kids' lives and preparing them for the future.  Young Life leaders have been serving Fairfield County students for more than 40 years, offering adult role models, safe places for social fun, and information about the Christian faith in a clear, fun and respectful way. Young Life is for every kid regardless of their beliefs, background, or spiritual involvement. All leaders have been trained and screened to work with kids.

Young Life has thrived for more than six decades, and is currently represented in all 50 states, 800 communities and more than 45 foreign countries, reaching an estimated one million teenagers annually. Young Life offers local clubs and seasonal resort-style camping, and is known around the world as the organization that knows how to have fun.

description:
The Learning Lab is now enrolling for Fall Kindergarten Enrichment classes. Choose from 2, 3 or 4 day per week programs. title: Cougar Soccer Camp for boys and girls set for July 26-30
description:
The Cranford High School boys and girls soccer programs, in conjunction with Central Jersey Celtic F.A., present their 2010 Cougar Soccer Camp at Orange Avenue School fields during the week of July 26 through July 30. The camp will run from 9:00am-1:00pm and is open for all boys and girls in grades 1-8, from beginners to advanced.

Camp directors are Cranford boys Head Varsity coach Mike Curci, girls Head Varsity coach Jen Michewitz, and P.J. Keim, President of the Central Jersey F.A.

Curci, honored as 2007 Star-Ledger Coach of the Year in Union County, led the CHS boys' varsity team to the Union County Tournament Championship in 2009, the first in the 54-year history of the program. The Cougars also nailed down their third consecutive Mountain Valley Conference Championship, while posting a record-setting 22-1-2 mark, finishing with a # 7 ranking in the Star-Ledger final Top-20. The 2009 team closed the season at 15-6 despite the loss of seven starters to graduation. The 2008 squad finished 9-1 in conference play, and own a conference record of 28-2 over the last three seasons. The 2007 team also finished with 15 wins while posting the first championship of any kind in the fifty-year history of the program. Over the last two seasons, the Cougars are 52-11-3. Curci, entering his 6th season at CHS, began his coaching career by spending several years as an assistant to the legendary Gene Chyzowych of Columbia High School, the all-time winningest coach in state history. Curci led the Columbia J.V. to a 17-0 mark in his 2nd season there before taking over the varsity program at Livingston H.S. where the Lancers made the state tournament all five years while facing perennial powers Columbia, Seton Hall Prep and St. Benedict's. Curci's playing career includes a conference championship at Carteret High School, before becoming a four-year starter at midfield for Seton Hall University where he led the team in goals his junior season and was named captain his senior season. In Coach C.'s five years at the helm, Cranford has gone from 35 players to 90 student/athletes wearing the white, blue and gold at the varsity, J.V. and freshmen levels. The Cougars look forward to building on their county and conference championship seasons as they continue a tradition of excellence. Mike has called Cranford home for the past 20 years with his wife Sally and their four children.

Michewitz is entering her 3rd season as girls Head Varsity Soccer Coach at Cranford. She guided the Lady Cougars to the Union County Championship in 2009, posting victories over rivals Scotch Plains and Westfield in the final two county games en route to a 16-3 record. Michewitz is a graduate of Seton Hall University where she started on the women's soccer team as a defender all 74 games of her career and was a captain her junior and senior years. In 2002, she received honorable mention for the Freshmen All-American Team, and in 2007 she earned the "Woman of the Year" Award from Seton Hall University for her accomplishments in athletics, academics and community service. Jen grew up in Pottstown, PA where she was highly involved with the Eastern Pennsylvania Soccer Association, training youth teams and coaching soccer camps. She currently lives in Westfield and teaches math at Cranford High School.

PJ Keim is President of  Central Jersey Football Academy, which currently supplies trainers to many of the local soccer clubs. He has been coaching youth soccer for over 12 years. Keim is the head coach of the two-time state cup finalist CWS Red Devils. PJ has lived in Cranford for 18 years and is the father of three wonderful children.

Once again, Mark Dutton, of Central Jersey F.A., will join the camp as Director of Coaching. His goal is to provide a positive and safe learning environment for all ages to become stronger athletes. Mark has been running camps in the U.S. for the past 12 years. Former star CHS players will also be on-hand to share their expertise and skills.

For more information or for a camp brochure, please call Mike Curci at 908-294-2101 or PJ Keim at 908-591-6734, or email mscurci@aol.com. You can also go to www.cjceltic.com to register.

title: Cranford Soccer Club registration is now open
description:
Registration for the Fall 2010 and Spring 2011 Recreational and Intercounty Soccer season is now open for all interested players at www.cranfordsoccer.net.  Open Registration will close on August 11th, 2010.  All players who register before the deadline are guaranteed placement on a team.  All players registering after August 11th will be placed on a wait list.  The wait list registration period will run until August 27th at which point registration will be officially closed.  Registration for the Peanut Soccer Program (4 and 5 year olds) is not yet open.  We are in the process of assessing this program to determine the best day and time to hold these "sessions".  We will make an announcement once registration for this program is open. 

Program Descriptions

For more detailed information about each program, go to our website and click on the program links on the left side of the page.  Our website also has a very detailed list of contacts under the "Board of Directors" link.  The Program Coordinators will have answers to specific questions, but you can visit the website for general updates throughout the season.

Online Registration Only

Please note that the Cranford Soccer Club requires that all players to be registered using our secure and safe on-line access.  Payments can be made online using a credit card, but may also be made by check after the online registration is completed. If paying by check, please include a copy of the confirmation receipt received and ensure payment is sent within 5 days of your registration or the registration will become invalid. For those who do not have Internet access, please visit our local library. NO MANUAL FORMS WILL BE ACCEPTED.

About the Cranford Soccer Club

The Cranford Soccer Club (CSC) was established in 1980 with the purpose to support the development of the sport of soccer for youths and adults in Cranford and the neighboring communities.  CSC organizes, sponsors and administers teams, competitions and programs to ensure the highest possible levels of soccer competence, sportsmanship and enjoyment.

Comments and suggestions are welcomed so that the Club may provide our children with the best opportunities available. Monthly Board meetings, held the first Wednesday of each month at 7:30 pm at the Cranford Community Center, are open to all.

title: Museum in the Streets Summer Program
description:
The Discovery Center's Museum in the Streets Summer Program

This program will run all summer long and is free and open to all to complete in their own time. The Museum in the Streets is a history walking tour of the Town of Ridgefield, CT. We hope this program encourages people to visit the Museum in the Streets plaques and that it will foster an appreciation of history and Ridgefield's unique past.   

To participate in this program please visit all thirty Museum in the Streets® plaques throughout Ridgefield to find the answers to the questions in our Museum in the Streets Quiz. The numbers of each plaque correspond to the numbered quiz questions.  

 To participate in this program you will need the Museum in the Streets Quiz and the Museum in the Streets Brochure with a map and locations of each plaque.  Both are available to download on our website www.ridgefielddiscovery.org or at Ridgefield Library.  

FOR COMPLETE DETAILS ABOUT THIS PROGRAM AND TO DOWNLOAD THE MUSEUM IN THE STREETS MATERIALS PLEASE VISIT OUR WEBSITE WWW.RIDGEFIELDDISCOVERY.ORG

Please send your completed quiz with correct answers to The Discovery Center by September 7, 2010 to be entered into a drawing for prizes. Please include your name, address, phone number, and email address so we may contact winners.  

Send completed quiz with your contact info to:  The Discovery Center, PO Box 926, Ridgefield, CT 06877 or email to info@ridgefielddiscovery.org  

Please contact us with questions at info@ridgefielddiscovery.org or 203-438-1063.  

BONUS: Email us your photos visiting the Museum in the Streets plaques to be posted on our Facebook page.  See who else is participating and join the fun!  

 Special thanks to Ridgefield Library, the Ridgefield Historical Society, and the Ridgefield 300th Anniversary Committee for making this program possible.

The Museum in the Streets is a Registered and Protected Trademark. For more information please visit www.themuseuminthetreets.com.
